title: Ze’iri (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He too was a Babylonian, Rav’s student, as is proven in Yevamot 21a: “Rav said: Four women … and Ze’iri adds: also his mother’s father’s wife.” So it is in Yuchasin that Ze’iri learned from Rav; and so it is cited in the Rosh, Bava Kamma, chapter 3, siman 7, that Rav was Ze’iri’s teacher.

Likewise we find “Ze’iri said that Rav Kahana said,” Bava Metzia 60b and Shabbat 7:2. He went up to the Land of Israel still in Rabbi Chanina’s lifetime, as we find “Ze’iri said that Rabbi Chanina said” in Shabbat 17a and 50a, Ketubot 15a, Sanhedrin 98a, Menachot 21a and 30b, and Niddah 19b. Likewise we find in the Jerusalem Talmud “Rabbi Ze’ira in the name of Rabbi Chanina,” as in Berakhot 5:2, Yoma 2:2 and Taanit 3:4, and Hyman considers him undoubtedly Ze’iri.

He was a distinguished student of Rabbi Yochanan, as in Kiddushin 71b: Ze’iri was avoiding Rabbi Yochanan, for Rabbi Yochanan used to say to him, “Marry my daughter.” One day they were walking on the road and came to a pool of water; he carried Rabbi Yochanan on his shoulder and took him across. He said to him: “Our Torah is fit, and our daughters are not fit?” In Avodah Zarah 53a: “Ze’iri said that Rabbi Yochanan said.”
In Yoma 9b, according to Rav Papa’s view: Resh Lakish was bathing in the Jordan; Ze’iri came and gave him his hand; he said to him: “By God, I hate you [Babylonians],” etc.

Afterward he went down to Babylonia, and this is what we find in Chullin 56a: “When Ze’iri went up (from Babylonia) to Nehardea” (Hyman explains this by saying that their route to the Land of Israel or from the Land of Israel was by way of Sura, which is Babylonia without further designation, and Sura lies below Nehardea, as in Taanit 10b; when Ze’iri came to Babylonia he came to Sura and afterward went up to Nehardea), he said: “But thus they said in Resh Lakish’s name.” There he was a colleague of Rav Nachman, as in Bava Batra 157a, where Rav Nachman called him “Ze’iri our colleague”; but Ze’iri was much older than Rav Nachman, and therefore we find in Avodah Zarah 61b, “Rav Nachman said that Ze’iri said.” Rav Huna’s great students spoke in his name, such as Rabbah and Rav Yosef, Nedarim 46a.

Likewise we find Abba bar Chanan in his name, Avodah Zarah 60b; Abba bar Rav Chisda, there 49b; Abba bar Chama, there 31a; and Surchav bar Pappa in his name, Ketubot 17b. Rava said that Ze’iri said, Sotah 5a, and Rava said of him, Zevachim 43b: “Every baraita that Ze’iri does not explain is not explained.”
He is mentioned in Gittin 87b, “Ze’iri taught,” and in Yoma 27b, “Ze’iri interpreted”; Hyman suggests that perhaps he is Rabbi Ze’ira the reciter mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1, folio 6b.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Yoma9b names RAV PAPA, supporting ר״פ; his alternative story has Ze’iri helping ReshLakish. אלהא is an oath invoking God, followed by hostility toward the Babylonian group, not an address saying God I hate you. The two alternative pairings are not silently merged. Tanna means reciter in the final possible Ze’ira identification. All geography and generation identifications remain Hyman’s.

The consulted Yoma 9b first pairs Resh Lakish with Rabbah bar bar Chana, then objects and gives Rav Papa’s alternatives: Resh Lakish with Ze’iri, or Rabbah bar bar Chana with Elazar. Hyman selects the former alternative; the versions are not merged. The invocation is an oath followed by hostility toward the Babylonian group. Geography, relative chronology, Ze’ira identity and final reciter equation remain Hyman’s qualified reconstructions.
